I'm writing the test first. The only file change is the new test file, and there is no production code to touch. The triage block is the contract here, so asserting on the text is appropriate. This is not the string-presence anti-pattern.

<edit path="tests/test_issue_templates.py">
import re
from pathlib import Path

TEMPLATE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / ".github" / "ISSUE_TEMPLATE"
TEMPLATE_NAMES = ["bug.md", "feature.md", "question.md", "docs.md"]
TRIAGE_BLOCK = re.compile(
    r"<!-- triage: begin -->.*?<!-- triage: end -->", re.DOTALL
)


def read_triage_block(name):
    text = (TEMPLATE_DIR / name).read_text().replace("\r\n", "\n")
    match = TRIAGE_BLOCK.search(text)
    assert match, f"{name}: no '<!-- triage: begin -->' ... '<!-- triage: end -->' block"
    return match.group(0)


def test_triage_blocks_are_identical_across_issue_templates():
    blocks = {name: read_triage_block(name) for name in TEMPLATE_NAMES}
    reference = blocks["bug.md"]
    drifted = [name for name, block in blocks.items() if block != reference]
    assert not drifted, (
        f"triage block differs from bug.md in: {', '.join(drifted)}\n"
        f"--- bug.md ---\n{reference}\n"
        + "".join(f"--- {n} ---\n{blocks[n]}\n" for n in drifted)
    )
</edit>

Because the templates are probably in sync now, the test may pass on its first run. To watch it fail, I'd temporarily introduce drift into a template, backing it up first.

<command>

sed -i '' 's/\*\*Priority:\*\* p3/**Priority:** p1/' .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/docs.md
uv run pytest tests/test_issue_templates.py -v
</command>

I expect a failure, with the message naming `docs.md` and showing both blocks. That would be a real assertion failure, not an import error or a typo. If the test still passes, the `sed` didn't match and I'd fix the mutation before going on.

Then I'd restore the template and confirm it is byte-identical to the original:

<command>

cmp /tmp/docs.md.bak .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/docs.md && echo restored
uv run pytest tests/test_issue_templates.py -v
</command>
